c:client_get_options.why: reads back the options a client was created with. `nros_client_options_t` ships and `nros_client_init_with_options` takes it; what is missing is the READBACK -- no `*_get_options` exists anywhere in our C surface, for any entity. CORRECTED 2026-09-04 (phase-417): this row said there is no runtime options struct. Seven ship and the correlator buckets all fourteen items `same` -- `nros_{node,publisher,subscription,service,client,action_client,action_server}_options_t` (`packages/api/nros-c/include/nros/nros_generated.h:1461,1729,2011,2474,2537,2556,2592`) plus a `*_get_default_options` for each, and `nros_node_options_t::domain_id_override` is a RUNTIME per-node domain. What is genuinely absent is the LIFECYCLE around one: no `*_options_copy`, no `*_options_fini`, and no `*_get_options` readback anywhere in the C surface.

c:client_init.why: phase-428 Q1 (2026-09-06) -- `rcl_client_init(client, node, type_support, service_name, options)`. No symbol answers to this key; the rclc spelling `rclc_client_init_default` does (`c:client_init_default`, `packages/api/nros-c/src/service.rs:1164`), and the options-shaped forms are `nros_client_init_with_qos` / `_with_options` / `_polling` (`packages/api/nros-c/include/nros/nros_generated.h:6448`, `:6470`, `:6519`). Same reasoning as `c:service_init`, one entity over.

phase-428 W5 (2026-09-06) — ledgering a recorded sweep finding. RANKED-14, CORRECTED — the finding as recorded said six `*_get_actual_qos` implementations "echo the request", and that headline is FALSE for this checkout. `read_entity_qos` (`packages/rmw/cyclonedds/nros-rmw-cyclonedds/src/qos.cpp:140`) does a REAL read-back: `dds_get_qos` then `dds_qget_{reliability,durability,history,deadline,lifespan,liveliness}` (issue 0823 / phase-393 W1), and all six thunks call it.

THE DEFENSIBLE STATEMENT IS NARROWER AND STILL A DIVERGENCE. `out` arrives PRE-LOADED with the request — the caller does `let mut granted = qos_struct;` before invoking the slot (`packages/rmw/cffi/src/lib.rs`) — and `read_entity_qos` overwrites only the fields whose `dds_qget_*` returns true. So every field Cyclone CANNOT report reads back as the REQUESTED value. Upstream's `rmw/rmw.h` requires `*_UNKNOWN` for exactly that case, and the one consumer compares requested against granted — so an unreportable field reads as GRANTED, the inverse of upstream's meaning. The code says so itself at `qos.cpp:134` and the header repeats it at `packages/core/nros-rmw-abi/include/nros/rmw_entity.h` (that header sentence is now itself imprecise, since the REPORTABLE fields no longer echo).

THE `*_UNKNOWN` SUB-CLAIM IS CONFIRMED BY GREP: the only non-test writes of any `*_UNKNOWN` value in the tree are in the graph endpoint-info trampoline (`packages/rmw/cffi/src/rust_adapter.rs`), NOT a `get_actual_qos`. No `*_get_actual_qos` implementation anywhere writes one — the slots whose own documentation defines the contract are exactly the ones that do not honour it. Every backend other than Cyclone leaves the six slots NULL.

HOW A USER FINDS OUT: this row's `gap` verdict already says the READBACK is not exposed to a C or C++ caller, so today nobody can observe it — a Rust user cannot reach it at all (`grep -rn actual_qos` over the facade and the node handles finds nothing; the read-back is consumed only by `report_qos_downgrade`). That is what makes this the moment to record it: closing the gap by surfacing the accessor would ship the inverted meaning to users, so the disposition ADOPT covers BOTH halves — expose the accessor AND write `*_UNKNOWN` for a policy the backend cannot report. Re-verified by hand against the current worktree before this row was written.

rename.resolution:
Target and shape settled 2026-09-03 by phase-379 W6 decision 2, which amended RFC-0036: "C keeps rcl's literal shape, `nros_ret_t f(args…, T *out)`". One C symbol, `nros_ret_t nros_client_service_is_ready(client, bool *out)`, with the tri-state `-1` arm becoming `NROS_RET_UNSUPPORTED`. C++ and Rust landed in 3941b569a; C is the open residue of issue 1008.

IT IS A SWAP, NOT A RENAME, and nobody had written that down: the target name is ALREADY TAKEN by a differently-shaped function — `bool nros_client_service_is_ready(const client)` (`nros_generated.h:6176`) — while the tri-state lives at `nros_client_server_available(client, int32_t *out)` (`:6141`). So `server_available` loses its name, the bare-bool loses its shape, and the deprecated forwarder must be written for the spelling that is KEEPING its name. Same collision class as `make_publisher`->`create_publisher` (issue 0818), one entity over.

c:client_service_is_ready.why: the correctly-named half of `c:client_server_available`, present only in C. Keeping both is the defect; see that row.

c:client_set_response_callback.why: the reply arrives at a callback bound to the CLIENT at creation, rather than resolving a future. `executor-owns-no-entity-storage` and RFC-0041, on the client side.

c:client_set_timeout.why: a per-client default deadline for a pending request, so a device that must not wait forever states the bound once rather than at every call. rclcpp has no client-level timeout -- the caller passes one to `spin_until_future_complete` each time.

c:client_try_recv_reply_raw.why: DEPRECATED SPELLING as of phase-379 W6 decision 1 (2026-09-03); the live name is `nros_client_take_response_raw` and the forwarder is a NROS_DEPRECATED_MSG `static inline` in the hand-written module header, so it adds no exported symbol and no ABI cost. Still on the surface, so still a row. Retired in W7 step 4, in one batch with the rest of the deprecated set. See `c:take`.

c:client_wait_for_service.why: blocks until the server appears or the deadline passes, driving the executor. rclcpp's `Client::wait_for_service` folds onto ours by the *Base rule; C's rclc has no counterpart.

c:executor_add_service_raw.why:
phase-417 stage 6 — the callback moved OFF `*_init` and onto registration, so `rclc_{subscription,service}_init_default` now matches rclc's four-argument shape and the callback arrives here, exactly as rclc supplies it at `rclc_executor_add_subscription`.

It keeps the `nros_` prefix DELIBERATELY, and that is the whole content of this row. rclc's same-named calls deliver a DESERIALISED message into caller-owned storage; these deliver CDR BYTES. Taking rclc's spelling for a byte-oriented entry point would be a name whose contract differs -- the `PollingSubscription::take()` failure, which had rclcpp's name, rclcpp's signature and the opposite contract, and cost a spinning loop with no compile error.

The faithful rclc-shaped entry point exists beside it and DOES take the name: `nros_executor_add_subscription_typed` (W5.a), reached per-message as `<Msg>_executor_add_subscription(exec, sub, &msg, cb, ctx, invocation)` -- rclc's six arguments in rclc's order. So the two shapes are distinguished by NAME rather than by a reader noticing which one deserialises, which is what RFC-0089 asks for.

c:send_request.why:
CORRECTED 2026-08-26 (phase-379 W5), re-verdicted rename -> divergence, with two factual errors fixed.
(1) There is no bare `nros_client_send_request` -- the brace spelling `nros_client_send_request{,_async,_raw}` claimed one. Verified word-boundary, repo-wide: the C API ships exactly `nros_client_send_request_async(client, request_data, request_len)` (executor-registered client) and `nros_client_send_request_raw(client, data, len)` (L1 polling-mode client). The `_async` / `_raw` split is two client MODES, not two spellings of one call.
(2) 'only the free-function shape differs' is wrong the same way `c:publish` was: both of ours ARE free functions taking the client first, exactly rcl's shape. `nros_client_` is a module prefix -- rcl uses the identical construction for `rcl_client_fini` / `rcl_client_request_publisher_get_actual_qos`. And the chain of precedent argues the other way in any case: `c:get_zero_initialized_client` defers to `c:get_zero_initialized_publisher`, which is verdict DECLINED, i.e. it argues for KEEPING our spelling.
What actually differs, and the constraint for each: `rcl_send_request(client, ros_request, sequence_number)` takes a typed `const void *` plus an OUT sequence number. Ours take bytes (`const uint8_t *`, `size_t`) because there is no runtime typesupport dispatch and no allocator to serialize into -- the same reason `c:publish` splits. And neither returns a sequence number because a nano-ros client keeps ONE call in flight (the `in_flight` flag and `reset_in_flight()` on the handle, `nros-node/src/executor/handles.rs`) rather than a correlation table; the backend does hand one back since issue 0778 and the raw handle drops it explicitly rather than by omission. Correlating replies across a client restart is the `rust:RequestId` divergence, one layer down.

rename.resolution: Not a rename. The word `send_request` already matches and so does the free-function shape; the row's remaining argument rested on a symbol spelling that does not exist and on a precedent that is itself `declined`. Re-verdicted to divergence naming the real differences (bytes not `const void *`; no out sequence number, one call in flight). No code change; no target name invented.

c:send_response.why:
RETRACTED as a rename 2026-09-04; re-verdicted `divergence`. Not an `extension` either — `rcl_send_response(service, rmw_request_id_t*, void*)` exists (`rclc.json`, `rcl/service.h`).

The row said ours is "method-style". It is not: `nros_service_send_response_raw(service, sequence_number, data, len)` (`nros_generated.h:5917`) is a FREE FUNCTION taking the service first — rcl's own shape — and `nros_service_` is a module prefix of the construction rcl itself uses (`rcl_client_fini`). This is verbatim the correction already applied to `c:publish` and `c:send_request` on 2026-08-26, and to the receive-side twins `c:take_request`/`c:take_response` on 2026-09-03. This row is the reply-side member of that family and was not swept with it.

What actually differs: `rmw_request_id_t*` (16-byte writer GUID plus sequence) versus a bare `int64_t` — the divergence written up at `rust:RequestId` — and a typed `void*` versus `const uint8_t*` plus `size_t`, because there is no runtime typesupport dispatch and no allocator. The `_raw` suffix belongs to the separate open SERIALIZED-vs-RAW question that `c:publish` owns, not to this row.

rename.resolution: Retracted 2026-09-04 as the fourth member of the c:publish / c:send_request / c:take_* family, all corrected earlier.

phase-428 Q1 (2026-09-06) -- `rcl_service_init(service, node, type_support, service_name, options)`. No symbol answers to this key. The six-argument `nros_service_init` (callback and context in positions 5 and 6) was retired at phase-417 stage 6 step B (`packages/api/nros-c/src/service.rs:303-322`): the callback moved to registration, where rclc puts it (`nros_executor_add_service_raw` <-> `rclc_executor_add_service`). c:service_init_default.why:
see `c:client_init_default`.

phase-428 Q1 (2026-09-06) — refuse-loud -> adopt-bounded. `rclc_service_init_default` EXISTS at rclc's arity (`packages/api/nros-c/src/service.rs:325`: service, node, type, name) and the correlator files it `same`; the old row promised a refusal nothing emits.

WHAT THE COMPILER POINTS AT: argument 3. rclc takes `const rosidl_service_type_support_t*` and a ported file passes `ROSIDL_GET_SRV_TYPE_SUPPORT(pkg, srv, Name)`; ours takes `const struct nros_service_type_t*` (the generated `<name>_type` descriptor, e.g. `&add_two_ints_type` in `examples/threadx-linux/c/service-server/src/main.c:138`). An rcl typesupport pointer at that position is an incompatible-pointer diagnostic on the call, naming both types. That is a mechanical edit, not a message with the migration attached, which is why this is adopt-bounded and not refuse-loud.

THE ENVELOPE: the callback is not on this call in either library — rclc supplies it at `rclc_executor_add_service`, ours at `nros_executor_add_service_raw` (`packages/api/nros-c/include/nros/nros_generated.h:4942`), so that half ports one-for-one. The service-name expansion caveat in `c:publisher_init` does not apply: services reach `resolve_entity_name` at registration.
